commodity_commentary: The Strait of Hormuz closure drove WTI crude above $100/bbl for the first time since July 2022, producing the most significant commodity repricing event of the current cycle and placing the database's 63 oil and gas projects directly in scope.1 Energy dominated March commodity performance, with WTI gaining more than 50% month-over-month and Brent recording its largest monthly gain since contract inception in 1988. Gold recorded its steepest monthly decline since October 2008 — down 14% from a peak of US$5,161/oz on March 3 to US$4,578 by month-end — as margin liquidation and US dollar strength overwhelmed safe-haven demand.2 Base metals were mixed, with copper holding its range and nickel declining, while agricultural commodities remained broadly stable. The database tracks 364 mining projects with direct commodity price exposure.3
wcs_analysis: The Western Canadian Select differential narrowed to approximately US$2.50/bbl below WTI as of March 27, compared to the 12-month average of approximately US$9.95/bbl. The narrow differential reflects elevated North American refinery demand for non-Hormuz crude during the supply disruption, which reduces the typical pricing disadvantage for Canadian heavy oil producers. The TMX pipeline, operational since May 2024, provides Alberta producers with Pacific Coast access at 890,000 b/d capacity, supporting crude export alternatives independent of the Gulf Coast market.4

commodities.name: WTI Crude Oil
commodities.commentary: WTI settled at US$102.88/bbl on March 31 — its first close above $100 since July 2022 — driven by the ongoing Strait of Hormuz closure that has disrupted an estimated 20 million barrels per day of seaborne oil flows.1 The database tracks 63 oil and gas projects and 727 Alberta projects with direct exposure to this price environment.

commodities.name: Western Canadian Select (WCS)
commodities.commentary: WCS traded at approximately US$97.14/bbl on March 27, reflecting a narrow US$2.50 differential below WTI compared to the 12-month average differential of approximately US$9.95/bbl.4 The narrow discount reflects elevated North American demand for non-Hormuz crude; Alberta oil sands producers with TMX pipeline access to Pacific Coast markets benefit from an additional export option.

commodities.name: Brent Crude
commodities.commentary: Brent crude closed at US$112.78/bbl on March 31, recording its largest monthly percentage gain since contract inception in 1988 as the Hormuz supply disruption affected a greater share of Brent-priced flows.1 The Brent-WTI spread of approximately US$9.90 reflects the differential impact of the disruption on international versus North American crude benchmarks.

commodities.name: Natural Gas (Henry Hub)
commodities.commentary: Henry Hub natural gas prices held at approximately US$3.05/MMBtu in late March, with the EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook projecting an average of US$3.80/MMBtu for 2026.5 AECO prices remained elevated on global supply tightness; BC LNG project economics and Alberta gas production operations are tracked through the oil and gas project segment of the database.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.commentary: Gold declined to approximately US$4,578/oz by month-end, its steepest monthly drop since October 2008, falling from a peak of US$5,161/oz on March 3 as margin calls and US dollar strength drove sellers.2 The 364 mining projects in the database include concentrations in British Columbia, Ontario, and Quebec, where gold mine expansion economics are sensitive to sustained price levels.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.commentary: Silver traded at approximately US$73.33/oz as of March 25, declining month-over-month alongside gold as precious metals broadly repriced in the second half of March.6 Ontario and British Columbia silver-bearing mining projects in the database share exposure to the broader precious metals price environment.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.commentary: Copper traded in a US$5.25 to US$6.01/lb range through March, with mixed signals from China PMI recovery and US tariff uncertainty preventing a clear directional move.7 British Columbia copper mining projects — the largest cluster of copper-linked projects in the database — and grid electrification projects with copper input cost exposure are tracked in the mining and power/energy sectors.

commodities.name: Uranium (URA ETF / CCO.TO)
commodities.commentary: The URA ETF uranium proxy closed at US$46.86, declining 2.8% week-over-week and 17.0% month-over-month alongside broader risk-off sentiment in metals, while Cameco (CCO.TO) closed at C$147.75, down 14.1% month-over-month.8 Saskatchewan uranium operations — including Cameco's McArthur River and Cigar Lake mines — represent the primary North American uranium production base; physical uranium spot prices (approximately US$92/lb) remain above the $65-70 mine operating cost range cited in Cameco's annual filings.

commodities.name: Nickel
commodities.commentary: LME nickel traded at approximately US$14,641/MT in late March, declining month-over-month amid weak demand signals from battery supply chain markets.9 Ontario and Manitoba nickel projects — including the Vale Voisey's Bay processing expansion and Sudbury operations — and battery supply chain projects in the database carry exposure to nickel price levels.

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.commentary: Wheat futures held at approximately 607.5 cents per bushel ($6.075/bu) in mid-to-late March, with prices stable following earlier seasonal adjustments.10 Prairie grain storage and handling infrastructure projects in the database are tracked under the agriculture sector; wheat prices at current levels are consistent with the feasibility economics of grain terminal expansion projects tracked in Saskatchewan and Manitoba.

commodities.name: Canola
commodities.commentary: Canola futures traded at approximately C$633/MT in late March, reflecting stable Prairie oilseed demand and refinery consumption.11 Saskatchewan and Manitoba canola crushing capacity projects tracked in the database depend on the sustained margin between canola and canola oil/meal prices; the current level is broadly consistent with reported crush margin feasibility thresholds.

commodities.name: Potash (Nutrien NTR proxy)
commodities.commentary: Nutrien (NTR.TO) closed at C$104.62, down 1.0% week-over-week and up 1.0% month-over-month, as a proxy for Saskatchewan potash mine operating conditions.12 Mosaic and Nutrien's Saskatchewan operations — tracked in the database under the mining sector — represent the world's largest potash-producing basin; muriate of potash (MOP) spot prices of approximately US$455/MT are consistent with the economics reported in recent expansion announcements.

commodities.name: Lumber (Random Length)
commodities.commentary: Lumber futures data was limited in coverage through the week of March 30, with available pricing indicating approximately US$510/MBF based on early March data; current real-time lumber data was not obtained in this pipeline run.13 British Columbia forestry projects and residential construction projects (211 tracked in the database) carry exposure to lumber pricing; US tariffs on Canadian lumber products remain a material factor for BC softwood producers.
